claims.text: Discrimination-aware classification can be achieved without requiring data modification.
Discrimination-aware classification can be achieved without requiring classifier tweaking.
The reject option of probabilistic classifiers can be exploited to reduce discrimination in classification.
The disagreement region of general classifier ensembles can be exploited to reduce discrimination in classification.
Discrimination reduction solutions using reject options and ensemble disagreement regions can be framed within decision theory.

evidence.description: In this paper, we present two solutions for discrimination-aware classification that neither require data modification nor classifier tweaking.
In this paper, we present two solutions for discrimination-aware classification that neither require data modification nor classifier tweaking.
Our first and second solutions exploit, respectively, the reject option of probabilistic classifier(s) and the disagreement region of general classifier ensembles to reduce discrimination.
Our first and second solutions exploit, respectively, the reject option of probabilistic classifier(s) and the disagreement region of general classifier ensembles to reduce discrimination.
We relate both solutions with decision theory for better understanding of the process.

methodologies.name: Reject option probabilistic classification for discrimination reduction
methodologies.description: A method exploiting the reject option of probabilistic classifiers to reduce social discrimination without modifying training data or tweaking algorithms.

methodologies.name: Ensemble disagreement region classification for discrimination reduction
methodologies.description: A method exploiting the disagreement region of general classifier ensembles to achieve discrimination-aware classification.

limitations.text: Prior methods for discrimination-aware classification require either modifying discriminatory data or tweaking a specific classification algorithm.
Prior methods for discrimination-aware classification are not flexible with respect to discrimination control and handling multiple sensitive attributes.
